verse.reading: We will turn the three worlds that cannot be described into red gold, make the hot sun's rays cool, and make this great world not exist; see our power and dance.
verse.nuance: Turning the worlds to gold extends the alchemist's transmutation to the cosmos; making the world not exist is read traditionally as the jnani's dissolving of the world in the void, as well as a feat of illusion.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: The poet says he abased himself as 'the knowing lame one', Nondi; he knew the fitting state and the clarity of the form of Parabrahman that the guru told.
verse.nuance: The unit has three lines; the heading 'I destroyed ego: the true state' is its missing first line. சிறந்து இழித்தேன் is a paradox, 'I excelled in lowering myself', and the name நொண்டி (lame) is taken as that self-abasement; it may also name the limping சிந்து metre of the song.

finding.claim: Loss of the sense of self in deep meditation and high-dose psychedelic states takes several distinct forms and is mostly reported by very experienced meditators or at high doses.

verse.reading: Before Death comes, before the eyes film over, before the milk you drink runs out at the corners of the mouth, before the kin fall on you and weep, before the townsfolk burn you: speak the name of the Lord of Kutralam.
verse.nuance: Five முன்னே, before, running from the far (Death's approach) to the near (the mouth that can no longer hold milk) and then past death to the mourners and the pyre. The thing to do in time is the smallest possible act, saying a name.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: The letter Sivayam is the letter in which Siva dwells, the true letter to trust as the means; the breath that has gone out through the doorless gate, the five letters Sivaya will call back by that means.
verse.nuance: கபாடமற்ற வாசல் (the gate with no door) is taken as the nostrils or the opening at the crown through which the breath leaves. The claim that the mantra calls the departed breath back is read by tradition as the mantra governing the breath (vaasi) in life, or as restoring life; the verse states it flatly as உபாயம், the means.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: Perform siddhi with the root called 'I'; siddhi lies within the hundred and eight; the eight seats of the gods will dance, all the sixty-four herbs will dance, the trumpeted siddhis will dance in an instant; it is good to do it on the day of Revati, good on the eighth lunar day, and the one who does it in the waxing moon is a yogi.
verse.nuance: தானென்ற மூலம், the root mantra called 'I' or 'that', is left unexplained. The powers promised are the eight siddhis (அண்டர் பதி எட்டு) and command over the sixty-four herbs of the medical siddhas. The timing by star, tithi and fortnight is the astrological frame the Siddhars share with the Tirumanthiram's breath-calendar.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: In the chakra of the worlds, in the space of the lord of the elements, the wind packed within the fire of the swelling lamp; at the gate where the two, sun and moon, move, changing the staff and climbing up, in the sporting space ...
verse.nuance: The stanza has no finite verb and seems to be the first half of a sentence that 1291 finishes. தவன and சோமன், sun and moon, are the right and left channels on the yogic reading tradition gives; தண்டு, the staff, is the spine; the space where the two play is the central channel. The wind packed in fire is the breath held at the root.

finding.claim: An underground radiation experiment ruled out the simplest parameter-free version of the gravity-related collapse model that Orch-OR depends on.

verse.reading: After praising the Lord of Pugali whose fame shone in the twelve ages past under different names, the bull-rider, husband of Uma, who bent the mountain and burnt the three cities of the strong-shouldered demons, with young moon on his growing hair and the single eye in his forehead that glared at Kama, the beginning the gods do not know, the poet confesses: in my untaught heart base understanding followed me, and with the empty gaze that looks and forgets, each time I looked, everything everywhere, mine and others', the many that come to be and the many that perish, what goes, comes and passes, more numerous than the sand heaped in the clear-watered world, the non-existent seeming to be and the existent unseen, I lay for many days in darkness; and the way it shook me was like a man who cannot see with his eyes and reels, the pit becoming his road and the road a pit, stumbling without end from one into the other; so it came, until I gained by compassion your look of growing grace, and then everything appeared false to me and you alone, the rare one, appeared true: like the many carved and painted shapes a master painter drew to catch a likeness, which to those who run their hands over them all without stopping show themselves as one wall.
verse.nuance: Two images carry the verse: the blind man for whom pit and road exchange places, which is the unenlightened state, and the painted wall, which is the enlightened one: the painter's many figures differ to the eye but the hand that feels them finds one surface, so the many things are false and the one substrate true. இல்லன உளவாய் உள்ளன காணா is the plain statement of maya in the Vedantic sense. The prose line printed after the verse (சடமாகிய உடம்பு எனக் கொண்டு, கல்லா உடம்பு எனவும் பாடமோதுவர்) is an editor's note that some read கல்லா உடம்பு for கல்லா உளத்தின்.

finding.claim: A microtubule-stabilising drug delayed isoflurane-induced unconsciousness in rats, consistent with but not proof of a microtubule role in consciousness.

verse.reading: Within the worshipping thought, trusting Guhan and the five-handed one, seeking them at left and right as ours; seating our Lord and the Mother and the one in the middle; as a bee follows, the word follows on, and sloth departs.
verse.nuance: Murugan (குகன்) and Ganesha (ஐங்கரன்) at left and right, with the Lord and the Mother and a middle one (நடுவன்), reads in tradition as the three channels: the left and right nadis and the central one. The plain reading is a devotional placement of the family of Siva. தும்பிபோல வாசகம் (the word like a bee) may be the hum of the mantra.

finding.claim: Agreement between practitioners reading the pulse in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine is low to moderate, and the methods remain poorly standardised.

verse.reading: Will it be bound? At the gate of impurity, in the middle of the centre, by kundalini's vaasi, if one binds the eight and the four and reveres them, one can mount and ride.
verse.nuance: மலவாயில், the gate of impurity, is the body's lowest opening, so the centre is the muladhara of 2593. The eight and the four are not explained; tradition offers the eight petals and four petals of the lower lotuses, or the eight siddhis and four steps. The horse is bound where kundalini sleeps and ridden from there.

finding.claim: Loving-kindness and compassion meditation improve self-reported wellbeing and reduce distress in small to moderate degree.

verse.reading: Where the four inner instruments and the five senses they govern become one and stand composed, heart, you joined.
verse.nuance: நாலுவகைக் கரணம் are the four inner instruments (mind, intellect, will and ego) of the tattva scheme; நல்கு புலனைந்து are the five senses they give rise to or direct. The nine are not destroyed but made one and steadied (சீலமுற்று), which keeps the body's apparatus inside the union.

finding.claim: The insula integrates signals from inside the body into a felt sense of bodily state, and disturbed interoception is implicated in anxiety, depression and eating disorders.

verse.reading: Not carrying this leather bag of rice about and withering, when shall I throw off the filthy inert body and reach you?
verse.nuance: துருத்தி is a leather water-bag; filled with cooked rice it is the body, a skin full of food. சடம், the inert thing, is the body as mere matter, set against உனை, the one reached.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Shall I not see the ears where the makara earrings lie shining? Shall I not see the beauty of the peaked crown and the red matted hair?
verse.nuance: வள்ளை, the ear (from the creeper the ear is likened to), carries the மகரகுண்டலம்; சிகர முடி, the crown like a peak, and the செஞ்சடை complete the ascent of the form begun at the feet in 479.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: Not knowing the thought behind the rock salt that comes, humans eat and fall into strong deeds and die; though rock salt, white rock salt, comes in many kinds, think that it is in the inner mind.
verse.nuance: கல்லுப்பு (rock salt) is a common Siddhar cipher; tradition takes salt variously as a body-fluid, as the alchemical salt, or as the taste of the world one eats and dies of. The last line, that the salt is 'in the mind' (உள்ளமதில் உண்டு), argues against a literal mineral and for a cipher. The verse makes a claim about where the substance is, not a preparation.

finding.claim: Elemental, inorganic and organic mercury are toxic to the nervous system and kidneys, and no safe therapeutic role for ingested mercury is established.

verse.reading: Are the days got as a maimed body, hunched and blind, not enough? Are the days weakened by base food not enough?
verse.nuance: ஈனப் புசிப்பு, mean eating, is either poor food or food got meanly; the count now runs through conditions within a human life rather than through births.

finding.claim: The gut microbiota signals to the brain through immune, endocrine and vagal routes and affects stress responses and behaviour in animals; human causal evidence is still limited.

verse.reading: We will stop the wind in the coppersmith's cave, kindle fire in the blacksmith's forge, make gold on the head of those who spoke, make learning equal ... ; we will burn away the bond of women, see the mark of the true Thing and reach what we desired; not babbling, not babbling, staying still, we joined Parapara.
verse.nuance: கால் is both leg and wind: stopping it in the cave is the breath held. The smithy and gold-making are the alchemist's tools, which the stanza may mean literally or as inner work. Line four is obscure. The close, பன்னாதே, சும்மா இருந்து, puts silence above all the furnace-work.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: Those who say 'breath', those who say 'the heart', those who say 'the release called silence', those who say 'speech': they do not know your name.
verse.nuance: Four methods are named and set aside together: the breath (the Siddhars' own vaasi practice), the mind, silence taken as release, and speech (mantra and recitation). Silence is placed among the sayings, so even மோனம் is here something people 'say'. What they lack is உன்னுடைய பேர், your name, which the poem never supplies beyond the refrain.

finding.claim: Slow controlled breathing is associated with greater parasympathetic activity, more alpha power and lower arousal and anxiety, though most trials are small.

verse.reading: Give no room to the desire that wants; do not get bound within the pains of the body; do not take birth again; do not let go of love at the feet of the guru-teacher.
verse.nuance: Four -ாதே lines, the last turned positive by a double negative: the one thing not to give up is love for the guru's feet, the song's constant positive (2273, 2274, 2285).

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: The sky all around, demon, and all around in the grove of trees; the fruit the elephant ate is the truth, you have seen.
verse.nuance: வேழம் உண்ட கனி is the proverbial wood-apple hollowed by the வேழம் (the gloss reads it as a disease of the fruit, tradition as the elephant): whole outside, empty within. The stanza may say that the world ringed by sky is such a fruit, or that the truth itself is the hollow, the emptiness inside appearances; both readings suit the chapter.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: After praising the Lord of Pugali whose fame shone in the twelve ages past under different names, the bull-rider, husband of Uma, who bent the mountain and burnt the three cities of the strong-shouldered demons, with young moon on his growing hair and the single eye in his forehead that glared at Kama, the beginning the gods do not know, the poet confesses: in my untaught heart base understanding followed me, and with the empty gaze that looks and forgets, each time I looked, everything everywhere, mine and others', the many that come to be and the many that perish, what goes, comes and passes, more numerous than the sand heaped in the clear-watered world, the non-existent seeming to be and the existent unseen, I lay for many days in darkness; and the way it shook me was like a man who cannot see with his eyes and reels, the pit becoming his road and the road a pit, stumbling without end from one into the other; so it came, until I gained by compassion your look of growing grace, and then everything appeared false to me and you alone, the rare one, appeared true: like the many carved and painted shapes a master painter drew to catch a likeness, which to those who run their hands over them all without stopping show themselves as one wall.

The prose line printed after the verse (சடமாகிய உடம்பு எனக் கொண்டு, கல்லா உடம்பு எனவும் பாடமோதுவர்) is an editor's note that some read கல்லா உடம்பு for கல்லா உளத்தின்.

verse.reading: After it has dried, take it, son, and set it devotedly in a kasaputa fire; let it cool, and when you take it out it is a sindhuram of the colour of the dawn sun; smear an atom of it on every drug and set them in the puta: the nine metals yield, and the whole art called vedai is in your hands.
verse.nuance: செந்தூரம் is the red calcined product of Siddha chemistry; நவலோகம் the nine metals; the claim is a universal agent that transmutes. நீருமடா may mean the metals turn to liquid or lose their nature. Read as history of a claim, not as a method.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: In the tank of Kayampatti the white kasa root has sprouted; if one rises upright from the mouth-river, the body will not perish, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: காயாம்பட்டி reads as the 'village of the body' (காயம்), its tank a bodily place; காசாம் வேர், the root of the kasa (white-flowered) plant, is a herb or its cipher. வாயாற்றினின்று நிமிர்ந்தால், rising from the river of the mouth, may point to the turning of breath or nectar upward. The claim is the kalpa claim of an undying body, here located within.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: The silence of Vishnu who settles, the silence where Hara dwelt, the silence of the elements composed, the silence held, the speed that owns the eyelid, the silence of the shining crown: men who know themselves do not look upon the corpse.
verse.nuance: சடம், the inert thing, is the body; those who know themselves (தமையறிந்த) do not attend to it. இமையும் கொண்ட வேகம், the speed that has the eyelid, is the flash within a blink. The silences are listed as in 1303.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Look: rising at dawn, without hurry set the mind at the suzhumunai; when the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai that is the womb, standing within the uvula without wavering, see it subside within the suzhumunai; of the sixteen, the eight and the four and the three, without scattering, join as one and go.
verse.nuance: பரிதிமதி, the sun and moon, are the right and left breaths in the Siddhars' cipher, and their exchange at the central channel is the practice; a plain reading, that sunrise is the hour, is also present in உதயத்தில் எழுந்திருந்து. கருவான சுழுமுனை, the suzhumunai that is the womb or seed, repeats the run's link between the yogic centre and conception. The arithmetic of sixteen, eight, four and three is from 2432.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: You have mounted the breath, demon; will you not seek the thing of the sky? Even mounting the breath, I tell you, it will not come.
verse.nuance: வாசியில் ஏறுதல், riding the breath (or the horse, in the cipher), is the Siddhars' breath practice. The stanza grants that the demon has done it and denies that it brings வான்பொருள், the thing of the sky; the breath lore of 1688 is thereby set aside as a means.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
verse.nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: When will I stand without obstruction in the sushumna that moves between ida and pingala, and stay there unshaken?
verse.nuance: The three channels are named plainly, which makes this the key to the ciphered 144. சலித்தருப்பது is corrupt or unusual: சலித்து can mean to be wearied or to be shaken, so the sense is either 'to remain without being shaken' or, less likely, 'to stay there and tire'; தடை அறவே (without obstruction) favours the first.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: Dressed in your guise, polishing the vessels, with heaps of incense and lamps, you behave like men who have butchered a goat and shared out the pieces; you spread out all the copper you could hunt up in heaps and throw flowers at it: what kind of worship is that?
verse.nuance: The priests arranging their copper vessels and images are likened to butchers dividing a carcass; the comparison may also recall 1122's sacrifice. மின் துலக்கி is 'polishing to a shine' (the brass), or 'polishing lightning'. The copper that is 'hunted up' (தேடிவந்த) suggests the images are collected goods.

finding.claim: Siddha polyherbal decoctions such as Nilavembu and Kaba Sura Kudineer have been tested in few, small COVID-19 trials, with uncertain benefit beyond standard care.

verse.reading: How many men have dug the pit, how many have touched the breast, how many have pulled at the lip; day after day they speak lies: leave the foolish women of this earth and be saved, be saved, be saved.
verse.nuance: The three எத்தனை பேர் make the woman's body a shared thing, and the lies (பொய்) are what each man is told. உய்யடா repeated three times is the chapter's loudest line; the verse addresses men, and its target is the women who take many men, so it is about the courtesan rather than women as such, though it does not draw the line.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: To see in the inner gaze the light that passes beyond time and all its ages, the wonder beyond imagining, the subtle thing the great ones of the books have spoken: that is the task, herdsman.
verse.nuance: The verse does not reject books: the subtle thing is what the learned great ones said, but it is to be caught in the gaze (நோக்கம்), not in their words. காலாகாலம் may be 'time and the timeless' or 'time and death-time'; either way the light stands past it.

finding.claim: Nearly every cell keeps a roughly 24-hour molecular clock entrained by light, and misalignment of these clocks is linked to metabolic and mental illness.

verse.reading: Supreme, there is no separate fear for you and for me; standing with hand raised and folding the hands in worship are what I owe; Lord of glory whose head melted and gave nectar: the strength you gave me is Om Namasivaya.
verse.nuance: பயம் may be fear or fruit, so line 1 may say there is no separate fruit for you and me. சிரம் உருகி அமுதளித்த, the head melting and giving nectar, is read in tradition as the yogic nectar from the crown; it may also be the moon on Siva's head. The verse accepts outward worship, unusually for this poet.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: It is a five-headed serpent, demon, and the gain from it is small; our Lord, you have seen, is the one who cures this poison.
verse.nuance: The five-headed serpent is read by tradition either as the five senses, whose poison is desire, or as the coiled power with its five faces; ஆதாயம் கொஞ்சம் (little profit) fits the senses better. The Lord as antidote (விடந்தீர்க்கும்) recalls the Siva who drank poison, and 1642's warning against poison.

finding.claim: Maximum human lifespan appears to have plateaued near 115-125 years, and radical life extension in this century is judged implausible.

verse.reading: Not knowing the fierce science, they wander in the garb of the world; if one knows the seed of the soham, the alchemy becomes the sky-going, girl.
verse.nuance: சோச பீசம் is read as the seed-syllable (பீஜம்) of சோகம் (so'ham, 'I am He'), the breath-mantra of Vedantic yoga; a corrupt word may lie behind it. கேசரம் (khechara) is the siddhi of moving in space and the state of 2657; the alchemy that works is the inner one made by a syllable, which closes the part's argument.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: If you rise at dawn and cut the four bindings of the sedge sprouting in the root pond, you can live as a child and become the supreme Brahman; the feet of the poison-eating Lord and the Mother's feet are the truth.
verse.nuance: The root pond (மூலக் குளம்) is, in tradition, the muladhara, and the sedge that sprouts there the coiled power or the desires rooted in it; the four bindings are not fixed (the four faculties, or four states). காலமே means 'early' but also plays on கால், breath. The plain reading, weeding a pond at dawn, stands on its own as an image of daily discipline.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: Pingala is where the rechaka is; placing the growing puraka in the left, so as to hold it as kumbhaka in Nandi: is this not the Siva-gaze, jnana girl?
verse.nuance: Breath in by the left channel (இடம், idai), out by pingalai on the right, held 'in Nandi', the place of the guru at the brow of 2572. சிவநாட்டம், the Siva-gaze, makes the breath-hold and the fixed look one act.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: Because the dross of the salt changed as it oozed, before old age turns it to calx; by the salt this body hardens for crores of aeons, and in the vaasi that leaps at a word, the body.
verse.nuance: சுன்னம் (calx, the calcined ash) is an alchemical end-product and here what old age makes of the body; the salt properly treated is claimed to keep the body for கற்பாந்தம் கோடி, crores of kalpas. The last line brings in வாசி, the breath practice, so the hardened body is kept by breath as well as by salt; the syntax is broken and the reading is a reconstruction.

finding.claim: Elemental, inorganic and organic mercury are toxic to the nervous system and kidneys, and no safe therapeutic role for ingested mercury is established.

verse.reading: He is the one beyond speech and mind, in whom the mind dissolves; he is hard to look upon, the subtle one among the subtle.
verse.nuance: மனோலயன் may be 'he in whom the mind dissolves' or 'he who is the dissolving of mind'. நுண்ணியரில் நுண்ணியன் is the Siddhars' சூட்சம், the subtle thing within; 556 ends the part with the same claim in Sanskrit.

finding.claim: Calculated decoherence times for neural quantum states are far shorter than neural processing times, a central objection to quantum-brain theories.

verse.reading: Those who know themselves and live by it hide themselves; those who do not know themselves are the ones who show themselves off; such knowers do not think to cherish some other god, for they cherish the great light.
verse.nuance: The second half most naturally continues the self-knowers: the one who knows himself needs no separate god because the great light is already his object. It could also describe the show-offs as men who cherish nothing but display; the first reading fits the chapter.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: The sixty-four arts come to hand and the kalpa of knowledge comes and merges; the good siddhas and the freed said that such a one is a god.
verse.nuance: சஷ்டிவித்தை is the சதுஷ்ஷஷ்டி கலை, the sixty-four arts. ஞானக் கற்பம் uses the medical word kalpa for knowledge itself, the rejuvenation that is knowing; 2607 calls this kalpa the true one. The deifying of the adept is credited to the siddhas and muktas, not claimed by the poet.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: So through the yugas I have been on earth, how many crores of times; is there anyone who knows as I do? I became the beginning of the primal siddhi; when I went to Vimala's place he lifted me with joy and kissed me and told me to stay on Kailasa; I remained in the crow form.
verse.nuance: ஆதியென்ற சித்திக்கும் ஆதியானேன் claims that Kakapusundar is the origin of siddhi itself; the kiss from Siva makes him a child of the god rather than a pupil.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: The poet says he does not know the wealth of you who created yesterday and tomorrow as remembering and forgetting and stood as change.
verse.nuance: நேற்று என்றும் நாளை என்றும், yesterday and tomorrow, are made of memory and forgetting, so time is a work of the mind the Lord created; மாற்றம், change, is his form. Sivavakkiyar (971) uses the same pair, remembering and forgetting, for maya.

finding.claim: In two combined randomised trials, eight weeks of mindfulness training produced no structural brain changes compared with active and waitlist controls.
